traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

canopy.silhouette: weeping dark-green curtains on a tall trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Young rimu are unmistakable: a slender pyramid whose long branchlets hang straight down like a weeping willow, clothed in soft, sickle-shaped juvenile leaves 4-10 mm long, dark green, bronze or orange in sun. Grows 1-2 cm a year under canopy, 15-30 cm in the open, reaching 12 m tall while still only ~10 cm thick; the weeping habit gives way to short, scale-like adult leaves.
growth.source: Wikipedia Dacrydium cupressinum (35 m, to 60 m; 15-30 cm/yr height in the open, 1-2 cm in shade; lifespan 600-800, some ~1200 yr; juvenile pendulous foliage 4-10 mm; seeds ripen Mar-May 15-18 months after pollination; bird-dispersed; seeds dormant >= 30 d; seedlings need partial shade). First seed age estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (pollen cones 5-10 mm, yellow; the seed, 4-5 mm, dark brown-black, sits on a small red to deep-orange fleshy cup; ripe Mar-May, 15-18 months after pollination; eaten by kereru, tui and bellbirds; mast seeding with strong yearly swings). Pollination month, set, crop and decay estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny epigeal seedling with 3-4 needle-like cotyledons, only 3-5 cm tall after its first year, very often perched on rotting logs and stumps (nurse logs) in deep shade. Saplings are narrow, feathery cones of flat sprays of short needles, with the leader and branch tips drooping; they can wait for decades suppressed under the canopy.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 1 (Packee): cones regular from 25-30 yr, very shade tolerant, height/site-index tables, max age usually 400-500 yr (record >700); Wikipedia (trees >1,200 yr known, seedlings 3-5 cm after year one, saplings 50-120 cm/yr in light)

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (Packee): pollination mid-April to June, solitary pendent cones 19-32 mm maturing 120-160 days after pollination, seed ripe mid-late Sept, scales open late Oct, empty cones persist 2+ yr, 30-40 seeds per cone, heavy crops every 3-4 yr; Wikipedia (green cones ripen grey-brown). Crop per tree estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two roundish cotyledons, then small, thick, glossy, finely toothed evergreen leaves (2.5-4 cm) in two flat rows along zigzag twigs. In the open it grows fast into a narrow cone with a straight leader and fine, feathery, fan-like branch sprays; old trees become huge, with a tall straight bole and flat, layered, cloud-like crowns.
growth.source: Wikipedia Nothofagus dombeyi (evergreen, fast growing, to 45 m and 1.9 m diameter; leaves 25-40 mm, leathery, toothed; nut triangular 4-7 mm); Veblen et al. (Nothofagus as a light-demanding pioneer after landslides, volcanism and fire in Chile/Argentina); first seed age and lifespan estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (triangular nut 4-7 mm); Nothofagus: tiny wind-pollinated flowers in spring (Sep-Nov), males with red-tipped stamens, females in threes inside a small scaly cupule that splits in late summer to drop two winged three-angled nuts and one flat one; heavy mast years; timings and crop estimated

traits.trunk: hollow woody jointed culms in a clump
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings appear only after a rare mass flowering: grass-like tufts of a few thin culms 10-20 cm tall with small leaves; each year the clump sends up taller culms from spreading rhizomes. Mature culms 1-3 m, arching at the base under snow, with big oblong leaves crowded at the top; each new culm reaches full height in about 2 months of early summer.
growth.source: Makita 1992 Ecological Research (Sasa kurilensis is monocarpic: after mass flowering the stand dies and regrows from seedlings over one to two decades); Japanese bamboo literature (culms 1-3 m, shoots May-June, edible 'nemagari-dake'); flowering interval not known, estimated as many decades

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings after a mass flowering look like thin grass. The young clump makes new culms each season, at first thread-thin and short, each generation thicker and taller, and dense bunches of whiskery branchlets grow at every node. Colihue culms are solid, pale, erect and closely packed, to ~6 m.
growth.source: Wikipedia Chusquea culeou (culms to 6 m, solid; flowers after variable periods up to ~60 yr, then the plant dies after seeding); Pearson et al. 1994 and Marchesini et al. 2009 (2001 mass flowering in Patagonia, seedling recruitment); culm lifespan and culm_days estimated

traits.native_range: Acer circinatum, vine maple, Pacific NW, sprawling understory tree of moist conifer forest, 3-8 m — Wikipedia / USDA Pla
traits.trunk: short twisted trunk, heavy low limbs, wind-shaped
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two strap-shaped cotyledons, then pairs of small round leaves with 7-9 shallow lobes. Seedlings are rare; most young plants come from layered or sprouting stems, so the young shrub is a clump of thin green-barked stems. In shade the stems arch, sprawl and root where they touch the ground (vine-like); in sun it stays a compact upright shrub.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Acer circinatum (flowers Apr-Jun, probably before age 10; seed needs ~6 months chilling and germinates in spring; seedlings rare, spreads by layering and root-crown sprouts; shade tolerant; to 9 m); growth rate and stem ages estimated (clones persist much longer)

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Acer circinatum (loose drooping clusters from branchlet tips Apr-Jun, red-purple sepals and white petals; only a few flowers per cluster set fruit; rose-coloured double samaras 1.2-2.5 cm with wings spread flat, ripe Sep-Oct, dispersed to Nov; very poor seed producer)

epiphyte.name: Tree moss

growth.juvenile_note: A spore germinates into a green thread-like protonema on bark or rock, from which small leafy shoots bud. These grow into stiff, erect, frond-like shoots branched like a tiny fir tree ('abietina'), forming patches that spread up oak trunks; when dry each shoot curls downward like a clenched fist, and it uncurls green within minutes of rain.
growth.source: Wikipedia Dendroalsia (sole species; conspicuous, often covering whole oak trunks, also on rock; each stem curls like a clenched fist when dry; oak woodlands from Los Angeles County to Vancouver Island). Spore-to-shoot time, growth and ages estimated from pleurocarpous epiphytic mosses.

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators
